clue.text: Try and be wise best man somehow in big church

indicators.note: somehow says the letters of these words come together in some new order

parts.note: taken as written as part of the letters to be rearranged
taken as written as the rest of the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Advice to a royal best man to behave himself at the big church ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' only joins the two stretches of letters; TRY plus BEWISEBESTMAN, sixteen letters, rearranged by 'somehow' give the London church where the 2011 royal wedding took place.
explanation.definitionFit: The great abbey church at Westminster in London is one of the most famous large churches in Britain.

clue.text: Determination one must have in the morning as man getting married

parts.note: will is resolve or determination
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: The groom shows resolve on the morning of his wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: Prince William was the groom at the April 2011 royal wedding this puzzle celebrates.

clue.text: Delivers special greeting before start of service

parts.note: ave is a Latin word of greeting, as in Ave Maria

indicators.note: start of asks for only the opening letter of the word service

explanation.surface: Someone offers a special greeting just before a church service begins.
explanation.definitionFit: To save someone is to deliver or rescue them, as in being delivered from harm.

clue.text: My right position on the field as a camp follower

parts.note: taken as written
mid-on is a fielding position in cricket

explanation.surface: Someone says where they field in a match, apparently as a hanger-on.
explanation.walkthrough: MID-ON is a cricket fielding position, in front of the batsman on the leg side. A myrmidon is a devoted, unquestioning follower, after Achilles' warriors.
explanation.definitionFit: A myrmidon is a loyal henchman or hanger-on, much as a camp follower trails after an army or leader.

clue.text: Beautiful female, I love to be trailing after knight

indicators.note: trailing after says the pieces before it come behind the knight in the answer

parts.note: N is the chess notation for a knight
love is nil, the letter O, in tennis scores

explanation.surface: A lovely woman longs to follow behind a knight in armour.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Niobe was a queen famed for her beauty and her many fine children, whose boast brought her ruin.

clue.text: English priest's embraced by Irish Father (the latter being this!)

explanation.surface: An English cleric is hugged by an Irish priest, whose show the clue hints at.
explanation.walkthrough: Father Ted was a hit Channel 4 sitcom about a hapless Irish priest; the bracket says the answer describes how it was shown, and the royal wedding too. 'embraced by' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Father Ted was broadcast on television, so 'this', the state the latter enjoyed, means shown on TV.

clue.text: No time for disloyalty — good sense needed

indicators.note: no time for says the letter standing for time is dropped from the next word

parts.note: treason is disloyalty to one's country or sovereign

explanation.surface: A comment that disloyalty has no place when sound judgement is required.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No time for' removes the T from TREASON.
explanation.definitionFit: Reason is the power of thinking sensibly, which is just what good sense describes.

clue.text: Honour is given to worker kowtowing maybe

parts.note: the OBE is a British honour, Officer of the Order of the British Empire
taken as written
a worker ant is the crossword's usual worker

explanation.surface: A labourer receives an award and bows low in gratitude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given to' is only a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Obeisant means showing deference by bowing, and kowtowing is one example of such deference.

clue.text: Shrub may rot losing middle bits and with leaves two-thirds gone

indicators.note: losing middle bits says each of the two short words drops its central letter

parts.note: taken as written before its middle goes
taken as written before its middle goes

indicators.note: two-thirds gone keeps only the first third of the six letters of leaves

explanation.surface: A gardener worries a shrub may rot with most of its foliage lost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing middle bits' strips A from MAY and O from ROT, giving MY and RT; 'two-thirds gone' leaves only LE of LEAVES.
explanation.definitionFit: Myrtle is an evergreen shrub with fragrant white flowers, traditional in royal wedding bouquets.

clue.text: Have fun attending player's last game for a top football club

parts.note: pool is a cue game played on a table

explanation.definitionFit: Liverpool is one of the most successful clubs in English football.

clue.text: See 1

clue.text: Very old catalogue includes one string player

parts.note: a list is a catalogue
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.walkthrough: 'includes' puts I after the V of VOLIST.
explanation.definitionFit: A violist plays the viola, a stringed instrument of the violin family.

clue.text: Instruments that could make old man sin

parts.note: taken as written as the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Musical instruments are blamed for leading an old man into sin.
explanation.definitionFit: Mandolins are plucked stringed musical instruments.

clue.text: No streets for a daughter to enter currently

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: to enter says the daughter letters go into the no-streets letters

parts.note: ways are roads or streets, as in highways

explanation.surface: A complaint that there are no streets a young woman can safely enter these days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to enter' signals the container; 'No streets' tempts a reading as a bare definition, but it is wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Nowadays means at the present time, just as currently does.

clue.text: I am married, I concede — one establishing new home?

taken as written
to grant is to concede or admit

explanation.surface: Someone admits they have married, perhaps to settle in a new country.
explanation.definitionFit: An immigrant is someone who settles in a new country, setting up home there; the question mark flags the loose description.

taken as written as part of the letters to be rearranged

taken as written as part of the letters to be rearranged

explanation.walkthrough: 'with' only joins the letters; KNOTTIEDLADME rearranged by 'contrived' gives the bride, and the whole clue is also her answer to 'Who?'.

clue.text: Terrible ordeal before party in fabulous place

indicators.note: terrible suggests the word ordeal is mangled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written as the letters to be rearranged
a do is a party or celebration

explanation.surface: A dreadful trial comes before the festivities in some legendary land.
explanation.definitionFit: El Dorado was the legendary city of gold sought by explorers, a mythical or fabled place.

clue.text: Lines of seats from which beautiful English girl is audible?

explanation.walkthrough: An 'English rose' is the British phrase for a classically pretty, fresh-faced English girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Rows are lines of seats, as in a theatre or church.

clue.text: Artist has turned up for prize

explanation.definitionFit: A reward is a prize given in recognition of something done.

clue.text: We start to dote adoringly — moved by this?

clue.text: A terrible moan by tortured soul would be unexpectedly odd
